known_anti_patterns: blast radius corrected upward: SIX copies of `project_key` exist, not two. scripts/effective-phase.py:47, scripts/phase.py:69, scripts/grant-actuation.py:56, scripts/actuation-intent.py:82, scripts/event-summary.py:50, scripts/loop.py:53
each copy keys the ledger by whatever cwd its command ran from, so a `cd` forks the ledger for one repository; four ledger directories exist today
roots.project_root() is the built fix and is wired into none of the six
any per-copy repair is a partial fix by construction: the ledgers only reconverge when all six agree, so five corrected copies leave the fork intact
roots.project_root() is now wired into project_key/project_directory directly, so all six callers inherit anchoring without per-caller edits (they already import from roots.py per commit 6e9b81a)

the pre-fix forked ledger directory (280f6a60fadbc82431436afd, the old subdirectory-cwd key) is not deleted or migrated by this fix -- it stops growing going forward but its prior contents are not reconciled into the repo-root ledger

grant-actuation.py is the sixth caller and is NOT covered by the new end-to-end test: reaching its project_directory read requires a live ferroplan-mcp verify_receipt round trip first, so it needs its own needs_cargo-marked test rather than being faked here

project_root() only anchors a checkout carrying the Ferroplan marker (crates/ferroplan-mcp/Cargo.toml) or an env-provided root related to the target path; a generic git-init fixture unrelated to Ferroplan does not get anchored at all and falls back to raw-realpath divergence -- confirmed by hand, which is why the new end-to-end test runs against the real checkout (root and plugins/chatman-ecosystem) under an isolated CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA rather than a synthetic git fixture

negative_falsifier.result: Stop hook blocked on 47 events in the plugins/chatman-ecosystem ledger while the repo ledger read 0 pending
negative_falsifier.why_this_counts: the defect demonstrated itself in the session that documented it -- an unambiguous, reproducible negative

positive_witness.why_this_counts: test_roots.py::test_project_key_is_identical_for_cwd_and_its_subdirectory proved only the shared primitive. This runs loop.py, phase.py, effective-phase.py, event-summary.py, and actuation-intent.py as real subprocesses -- the way hooks and the CLI actually invoke them -- firing hooks from plugins/chatman-ecosystem and reading state back from the repo root (and vice versa), against the real checkout so project_root() genuinely anchors. All five callers converge on one ledger directory: a mutation event counted from the subdirectory is visible to loop.py status and phase.py status run from the root, effective-phase.py's projection reflects it, event-summary.py's write lands in the same directory loop.py reads, and actuation-intent.py's BRCE refusal cites the exact pending count observed elsewhere.
